Theme

Latin word

animī

genitive of animus, after the noun

of the mind (as against the body); of the mind, mental

In this lexicon

  • intellectual

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Sen. 38: eās rēs tueor animī nōn corporis vīribus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Off. 1.123: exercitātiōnēs animī

Examples

  • senibus autem labōrēs corporis minuendī, exercitātiōnēs animī etiam augendae videntur

    for the old, bodily labour should be lessened, and exercise of the mind even increasedCic. Off. 1.123

    In the entry for intellectual

  • eās rēs tueor animī nōn corporis vīribus

    I keep up these things with the strength of my mind, not of my bodyCic. Sen. 38 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for intellectual

  • utrumque laetor, et sine dolōre corporis tē fuisse et animō valuisse

    I’m glad of both: that you were free of bodily pain, and that you were mentally soundCic. Fam. 7.1.1

    In the entry for mental

  • animī valentēs morbō tentārī nōn possunt, corpora possunt

    healthy minds cannot be attacked by disease; bodies canCic. Tusc. 4.31 (Lewis & Short)
